variantDescriptions.nodyn: base with `-XX:-UseDynamicNumberOfCompilerThreads`: compiler threads all start with the VM, so the global `os::random` sequence that seeds each thread's identity-hash state is consumed in a fixed order
variantDescriptions.hc3: base with `-XX:hashCode=3`: identity hashes from a global counter, so their order follows allocation order

name: m4-forkvar-hash
description: Does identity-hash nondeterminism drive fork-to-fork variance in the work the compiler does? `Symbol` has no `hashCode` override, and trees and some types hash by `System.identityHashCode`, so hash set/map iteration order over symbols, and probe lengths in the type unique table, can differ from fork to fork. Compare each variant's spread of instructions/op across forks; a smaller spread in `nodyn` or `hc3` points at the compiler's hash-dependent work, not the JIT. Means are not comparable across variants (both flags change hashing or JIT throughput).
